note: Draft register for Spec 053 (design D-07 arm A only, PR #195 packet), opened 2026-10-21 under the runnable-experiments campaign plan approved by the owner AS WRITTEN on 2026-10-21 (campaign member 6; decision E-3 keeps arm B out of this pass). Conventions as in Specs 032-048: requirement claims carry no falsification test where a gate or inspection is the operative check; boundaries carry the conditions under which each claim holds; evidence items carry observed_at from this draft because the cited facts were verified first-hand at drafting. The AEE lifecycle hooks have NOT run on this register; they are the freeze gate (tasks L4), and any recovery round they force changes claim text before any freeze digest is computed. ASM- ids name the assumptions each claim stands on: ASM-CLAIM-RECORD (the claim file as pinned is the record of the strongly supported verdict, its exponent, and its residue), ASM-STRICT-CORPUS (the strict corpus is the V3/Mahadevan-lineage corpus as held in the database, restricted to the strict sign set, identified and pinned at gate 0.3), ASM-ESTIMATOR (spec section 4.2's estimator is the fitting rule of record for every system), ASM-PUBLISHED-COUNTS (each control's published counts, entered whole at gate 0.4, are that system's inventory as its source reports it), ASM-SYNTHETIC-PROCESS (the Yule-Simon process pinned in spec gate 0.4 generates the synthetic control), ASM-GATES-BEFORE-OUTCOME (pins, frozen tables, and census precede any fit quantity), ASM-APPEND-ONLY (outcomes append; frozen records are never edited), ASM-ARM-B-CONTINGENT (arm B waits on its Phase-130 trigger and its own planning gate, per campaign E-3). FREEZE (2026-10-21): the AEE lifecycle hooks ran at the freeze act under aee 1.5.0; the full record is in aee/freeze-aee-note.md. Before the hooks ran, the freeze's own rulings were carried into the register: DD-053-11's estimator ruling (option (a) — spec section 4.2's estimator specified completely as the fitting rule of record, the 'identical to Phase-43' reading retired, Yadav's recorded value of about 1.35 carried as context only) into F053-C02's boundary, F053-C06 (text, boundary, alternatives) and F053-C11's boundary; DD-053-15 (epsilon = 0) into F053-C07's boundary; DD-053-13 (control sources as named, gate 0.4 as the fixed pin source for the control tables, no second positive control) into F053-C08's boundary; DD-053-12 (strict population and gate 0.3 confirmed) into F053-C09's boundary; DD-053-14 (floors 50 types / 2,000 tokens confirmed) into F053-C10's boundary; and the COMPARISON UNINFORMATIVE confirmation into F053-C12's boundary. Rounds at after_specify: a loadability recovery from 0.5-draft to 0.6-draft (every evidence item normalised to kind observed and source_quality artifact — the draft's free-form kind and source_quality labels are not engine values and the loader refuses them); 47 failure modes over 0.6-draft (13 irreducibility challenges recorded as coverage_gap, 19 shared-evidence independence-unmodelled records, 15 FR-2.3 draft-cap records; no claim below the 0.70 threshold, minimum propagated 0.72); a recovery to 0.7-draft restating the 13 challenged claim texts as single head propositions with their carried clauses moved into the boundaries verbatim-in-substance, and mutual independent_of declarations on every multi-item claim's evidence; one negation-conflict challenge over 0.7-draft (F053-C01 / F053-C04), adjudicated as no contradiction — C04 is the NOT SEPARABLE branch of C01's scope statement and the two share a boundary by design — with C04's head restated to name the firing falsifier as its subject and the adjudication recorded in its boundary; then 15 draft-cap records only, zero correctness failure modes, minimum propagated 0.72. after_plan and after_tasks clean at first pass on the same terms. The engine outcome word reads iterate solely from the draft-cap records (gate reading DD-053-19, adopting DD-038-10).

claims.text: An outcome under Spec 053 states only whether the Indus strict corpus's Zipf-Mandelbrot fit is separable, on the spec's stated measures, from the fits of the named non-linguistic control systems, under one identical estimator.
claims.boundary: The scope is the pinned strict corpus (the strict sign set's distribution in the V3/Mahadevan-lineage layer), the named control set of spec section 3 gate 0.4, and the estimator and comparison rule of spec section 4. It excludes any statement about whether the script encodes language, about what any sign means, about any non-linguistic system not named in the set, about Yadav's full-inventory population (addressed only as sensitivity S3), and about arm B (F053-C14).
alternatives: the recorded Phase-43 fit could be read as already answering the worth question (it cannot: it fitted one system and compared it to no control)
falsification_tests: the claim is falsified in scope if any Spec 053 output states a conclusion about a system, corpus, measure, or question outside the named-set comparison under spec section 4

metadata.strongest_rival: the alternative reading in which separability from the named controls licenses a claim about language, or non-separability licenses a claim that the script is not writing
metadata.verdict_rule: scope is judged by inspection of every Spec 053 output against this boundary; any output exceeding it is a defect of the output, recorded as such, not a finding

evidence.description: Claim record for yadav_2009_arxiv_manual_001 (SHA-256 90476623..., recomputed at this draft from main head 83b6a563...): normalized claim 'Indus script sign frequencies follow a Zipf-Mandelbrot distribution', status strongly_supported, stage explained, evidence string 'Phase-43: V3 Zipf exponent ~1.35 (super-Zipfian) [VERIFIED]', and the not-understood text naming the non-linguistic-systems comparison and the independent-corpus fit as the two strengthening acts.

Design D-07 (PR #195 packet, section D-07, read in full at this draft): hypothesis (the Indus fit is distinguishable from known non-linguistic systems), falsifier (at least one named non-linguistic system fits as well or better under the same fitting rules), arm A method (identical estimator on the strict corpus, at least three published non-linguistic inventories, at least one linguistic positive control, subsampling and split/merge sensitivity table), arm B blocked on an independent corpus, and the closing limit (arm A cannot promote the fit into language evidence; its product is a bounded finding, not a verdict change).

claims.text: yadav_2009_arxiv_manual_001 stands strongly supported on its recorded test.
claims.boundary: These are the claim record's own statements, read first-hand at this draft. The exponent is not corroborated by any Zipf entry in Phase-43's results file: outputs/phase43_all.json (pinned in spec section 2, read in full at this draft) carries the phase's corpus census and positional/SA tables and records no Zipf fit, and no Phase-43 Zipf estimator is pinnable on main at this draft (adjudication section 7, defect 2). The exponent is therefore context for this spec's comparison, not a reproduction target, and the full-inventory sensitivity S3 reports its fitted exponent beside this recorded value without adjudicating it. Ruled at the freeze (DD-053-11, option (a)): the 'identical to Phase-43' reading is RETIRED on the record — no Phase-43 Zipf estimator exists to be identical to — and this spec tests Yadav's recorded value of about 1.35 only as context under the named estimator of spec section 4.2, exactly as this claim's boundary already states. Carried from the draft text: Phase-43 fitted the V3 corpus; the recorded Zipf exponent is about 1.35; the claim's recorded falsifier is that the frequency distribution deviates from the Zipf-Mandelbrot law.
falsification_tests: recompute SHA-256 of the claim file (90476623...) and read manual_001's status, evidence string, and falsification_condition; any mismatch falsifies this statement and voids the draft's basis

claims.text: Every named non-linguistic control fits the Zipf-Mandelbrot curve strictly worse than the Indus strict corpus under the spec section 4 estimator.
claims.boundary: The hypothesis is a statement about these systems, this strict population, and these measures only. It asserts nothing about non-linguistic systems in general, nothing about the full Indus inventory (sensitivity S3), and nothing about language. The positive-control clause is the hypothesis's informativeness half (spec section 4.4); a failure of that clause routes the outcome to COMPARISON UNINFORMATIVE under F053-C12, not to support or refutation of the Indus half. Carried from the draft text: each control's NRMSE_log is strictly greater than the Indus NRMSE_log; the linguistic positive control fits strictly better than every non-linguistic control.
alternatives: at least one non-linguistic control fits as well or better (the falsifier, F053-C04)
the measures cannot rank the positive control above the non-linguistic controls (COMPARISON UNINFORMATIVE, F053-C12)
falsification_tests: run the section 4 fits: if any non-linguistic control's NRMSE_log is less than or equal to the Indus NRMSE_log, this hypothesis is not supported; if the positive control does not fit strictly better than every non-linguistic control, the comparison is uninformative and the hypothesis is not adjudicated

metadata.strongest_rival: the strongest rival is the falsifier itself: the curve is a generic shape that non-writing systems and random processes produce as well as the script does

claims.text: Every system in the comparison is fitted with the one estimator of spec section 4.2.
claims.boundary: Estimator identity is what makes the errors comparable. This estimator is the fitting rule of record for this spec (DD-053-3), confirmed complete at the freeze as a freeze-stage design decision (DD-053-11, option (a)): model f(r) = C / (r + q)^alpha with C fixed by normalisation (sum of fitted counts = N), minimising the sum of squared log residuals over alpha 0.00-3.00 in steps of 0.01 and q 0.0-20.0 in steps of 0.1, then one refinement pass at one-tenth steps around the best grid cell; primary quantity NRMSE_log; the gate 0.2 self-test uses the planted parameters alpha 1.20, q 2.0, V 200, N 50,000, seed 20261021. It is not Phase-43's estimator: Phase-43's results file (outputs/phase43_all.json, SHA-256 78a6c21908b9362854c54dd3d820d717be22feab3af11135663fa14aaf554fe4, verified at the freeze by two routes) records no Zipf fit — no exponent, no Mandelbrot parameters, no fitting procedure — and no Phase-43 Zipf estimator is on main. The 'identical to Phase-43' reading is therefore RETIRED at the freeze, honestly and on the record (DD-053-11); no substitution is possible after any fit exists. The gate 0.2 self-test is this claim's operational check. Carried from the draft text: that estimator is the Zipf-Mandelbrot model with normalisation-fixed C, fitted by minimising squared log residuals over the stated deterministic grid with its refinement pass; no other estimator is used for any reported fit quantity.
alternatives: recovering and reusing Phase-43's own estimator (ruled out at the freeze under DD-053-11: no such estimator exists on the record — Phase-43's results file carries no Zipf fit)
falsification_tests: gate 0.2 is the operational test: an implementation that cannot recover the planted parameters (alpha within 0.10, q within 1.0) stops the run as INVALID; any reported fit quantity produced by a different estimator falsifies the outcome record

metadata.strongest_rival: silent estimator drift between systems (a different grid, smoothing, or fitting space for one system) presenting as a separability result
metadata.verdict_rule: identity is judged by the gate 0.2 self-test plus the single implementation the execution record exhibits for all systems

claims.boundary: These are spec section 4.3's rules, fixed before any fitting. The verdict rule carries no tolerance band (DD-053-2): the design's words are 'as well or better', and the draft reads them literally. Secondary quantities (log-space R-squared, fitted alpha and q) are reported for every system and decide nothing. Confirmed at the freeze (DD-053-15): the verdict rule carries no tolerance band (epsilon = 0) and the 0.02 band stays reporting-only. Carried from the draft text: NRMSE_log is the root-mean-square log residual of the section 4.2 fit; a non-linguistic control fits as well iff its NRMSE_log is at or below the Indus strict corpus's NRMSE_log (for the synthetic control, its 99-replicate median); every control's gap against the Indus error is reported; a control with a gap in (0, 0.02] is named a NEAR MISS in every reporting product without affecting any verdict.
alternatives: a tolerance band inside the verdict rule (considered in the double derivation and refused for the verdict; retained as the reporting-only near-miss band)
falsification_tests: the outcome record's separability word must be derivable from the published per-system NRMSE_log values by this claim's rule alone; any word not so derivable falsifies the record

claims.text: The control set is exactly the systems named in spec section 3 gate 0.4.
claims.boundary: N1, N2, and P1 are their published sources' complete reported inventories, entered whole with citations and locators; no selection, trimming, or completion from another source. N3 is generated by the process pinned in the spec, not chosen after seeing fits. A second positive control may be added only at the freeze, openly. If any named system cannot be entered completely, the run closes CONTROL SET FREEZE FAILED (F053-C10) rather than proceeding on a reduced set. Ruled at the freeze (DD-053-13): the named systems and their bibliographic pins stand as drafted — N1 from Nissen, Damerow & Englund, Archaic Bookkeeping (1993) and the published archaic sign counts it reports; N2 from a published roll of arms; P1 Linear B from published corpus counts — no second positive control is added, and the exact tables and per-count locators are entered as cited data at gate 0.4, which is the fixed pin source for the control tables; a system that cannot be entered whole there closes the run CONTROL SET FREEZE FAILED, exactly as drafted. The freeze invents no table it has not seen (adjudication section 7, defect 4). Carried from the draft text: those systems are N1 Mesopotamian numerical-sign frequencies, N2 heraldic charge frequencies, N3 the synthetic emblem inventory generated by the pinned Yule-Simon process (innovation probability 0.10, seed 20261021, token total matched to the Indus strict total, 99 replicates), with P1 Linear B syllabic sign frequencies as the positive control; the set is entered as cited data and frozen before any fit of any system, the Indus included.
alternatives: a uniform-random synthetic inventory (refused in the double derivation: it is near-flat by construction and cannot test the residue's point)
substituting a more convenient control when a named source proves hard to enter (refused: the closure class exists for exactly that case)
falsification_tests: the step-0 record must exhibit the frozen tables with citations before the first fit quantity in the run record; a fit preceding the freeze, or a set differing from the named set, falsifies compliance

metadata.strongest_rival: control-shopping: choosing systems after seeing which ones fit well, or quietly dropping the control that fires the falsifier
metadata.verdict_rule: the frozen step-0 tables and their citations precede all fits in the run's own record, or the outcome is CONTROL SET FREEZE FAILED by construction

claims.text: Execution stops before any fit is computed when a spec section 3 gate fails.
claims.boundary: These are spec section 3's gates 0.1-0.5. Their failure classes are INVALID (0.1/0.2), STRICT CORPUS NOT PINNABLE (0.3), CONTROL SET FREEZE FAILED (0.4), and TOO THIN (0.5). The floor values are this draft's (DD-053-7), stated before any census exists; the freeze may adjust them openly, before execution, and not after. No failure is repaired at run time; a repaired input is a new freeze, not a resumed run. claims.text: The spec section 5 sensitivities are reported beside the primary outcome.
claims.boundary: Subsampling is at inscription level (DD-053-9): token-level sampling would fabricate texts that never existed. S2's variants are built from the pinned crosswalk's typed links before any variant fit is seen; a type whose components the corpus encoding does not carry is reported unexpanded by name and the variant labelled partial. No sensitivity outcome - however dramatic - moves the section 4.5 headline; a sensitivity that contradicts the primary is reported as contradicting it. Under DD-053-11 the S3 exponent is reported beside the recorded value of about 1.35 as context only; it neither reproduces nor contradicts a Phase-43 fit, because no Phase-43 fit is on the record. Carried from the draft text: the sensitivities are S1 subsampling (refits on random halves and quarters of inscriptions, 99 replicates per level, seed 20261021, median and central 90% interval of alpha and NRMSE_log per level), S2 split/merge variants constructed from the pinned crosswalk alone, with S3 the full-inventory fit reported beside the recorded exponent of about 1.35; no sensitivity changes any verdict.
alternatives: token-level subsampling (refused: it breaks inscription structure and understates the movement the sensitivity exists to measure)
falsification_tests: an execution record lacking any of S1-S3, or whose headline follows a sensitivity instead of the section 4 primary, falsifies compliance

claims.text: The headline is COMPARISON UNINFORMATIVE when the positive control fails its spec section 4.4 condition.
claims.boundary: COMPARISON UNINFORMATIVE is a finding about the measures, not about the script: the estimator and comparison quantity failed to rank the set's one certainly-linguistic system above its non-linguistic systems, so they are not used to judge the Indus fit. The Indus quantities are still reported for the record. This class is this draft's completion of the design's outcome set (DD-053-5), following Spec 042's NOT ADJUDICATED precedent; the freeze confirms or replaces it openly. Confirmed at the freeze (DD-053-19's companion ruling in adjudication section 8): COMPARISON UNINFORMATIVE stands as the positive-control-failure class.
